column6: ganita_paripurna_shesh(a, b)ganita_paripurna_shesh(a, b) — truncating a % b (WS4, R24). Remainder never overflows mathematically (INT64_MIN % -1 is exactly 0), but the hardware operation still traps on MIN % -1 (same SIGFPE as MIN / -1), so this guards that case and returns 0 — which is also the exact result. b == 0 returns 0 (same sentinel as sat_div). Guards before operating, so it never executes a trapping operation.

column6: layer: core FNV-1a (Fowler–Noll–Vo) 32-bit hash. Deterministic, fast, good distribution for non-cryptographic use (hash tables, checksums, dedup keys). Reference: http://www.isthe.com/chongo/tech/comp/fnv/ offset_basis = 2166136261 prime = 16777619 for each byte b: hash = (hash XOR b) * prime (shesh 2^32) fnv1a(s, len) — FNV-1a hash of the first len BYTES of a packed byte-string pointer s. Returns an unsigned 32-bit value in the integer range 0..4294967295.

column6: layer: core The string toolkit on BYTE-PACKED strings (the representation of a literal and of set_char-built buffers). Own module (not inside THE TWO REPRESENTATIONS (see also lib/varna.smlib): char-code array: qword cells, one char code per cell, h[i]. byte string: bytes packed 1-per-byte, char_at(s, i) / set_char(s, i, v) / vartani_aayam(s). Do NOT mix them: h[i] on a byte string reads 8 bytes at once; char_at on a char-code array reads one byte of a qword cell. Conventions: lengths are explicit; out-buffers get a 0 terminator; the caller allocates generously. Empty needle matches at 0; "not found" is -1. All signatures stay within the 6-argument cap. SLICE-BOUNDARY RULES (R23): a slice is (pointer, length) into a larger buffer, with NO terminator at the slice end. Explicit-length khand_* function takes an explicit length and stops at it. The NUL-terminated forms (anwesh_akshar, gan_akshar, gan_swar, asti_sarv_ank, varna_sam) scan to the terminator — WRONG on slices. khand_maap / varna_maap / vartani_aayam scan to the terminator and cannot be used on slices. khand_pratisthap's repl is 0-terminated (length derived), so repl cannot be a slice; khand_pratilip it into a terminated buffer first. khand_bhed/khand_yuj use the length-prefixed segment format of varna_bhed/varna_yuj (R9): [len0, b0, ..., len1, b0, ...]. khand_bandh(cells, n, out) — pack a qword-cell sequence (one byte value per cell, the varna_bhed/khand_bhed segment format) into contiguous bytes. Writes a 0 terminator at out[n]. Returns n. This is the boundary helper: hand-written repack loops (one per call site, each a chance to get the stride wrong) become one call. n <= 0 writes only the terminator and returns 0. POINTER ARITHMETIC IS IN BYTES: to pack starting at cell i of a cell array, pass cells + i*8, not cells + i.

column6: layer: alloc Open addressing with linear probing over parallel mala arrays. KEY REPRESENTATION: byte strings (the current khand_* byte surface), NOT char-code arrays: keys are usually literals ("apple"), and byte strings let the caller pass a literal directly. The hash (lib/gudh.smlib fnv1a) is byte-based (char_at), so the choice is consistent end to end. Do not pass char-code arrays here. Layout of the map buffer m (qword cells, except the key bytes): m[0] capacity m[1] live entry count m[2+i] state[i] (0 = empty, 1 = live), i in 0..cap-1 m[2+cap+i] keylen[i] m[2+2*cap+i] val[i] key bytes: byte region at byte offset (2+3*cap)*8, KEY_MAX bytes/slot. KEY_MAX = 32: keys longer than 32 bytes are truncated to 32, consistently on put/get/contains/remove (documented; excluded from the properties). cap must be >= 1 (clamped). Probing wraps modulo cap. DELETION is backward-shift (Knuth 6.4R): the freed slot is filled by shifting later probe-chain entries back toward their home bucket, so there is no "deleted" state and no tombstones — a lookup stops at the first empty slot and never misses a live entry. ABSENT SENTINEL: nighantu_grah returns -1 (0-1) for a missing key. Values are programmer-managed integers; do not store -1 as a value unless you disambiguate with nighantu_antah first. FULL TABLE: nighantu_khip returns 0 and changes nothing.

column6: nighantu_kunjika(m, out)nighantu_kunjika(m, out) — write live keys into out in length-prefixed form [len0, b0, b1, ..., len1, b0, ...] (same shape as varna_bhed parts). Returns the key count, which equals nighantu_maap(m). NOTE: segments are QWORD CELLS (len in one cell, one byte per cell), kept for backward compatibility. New code should use nighantu_kunjika_ashtak below, which returns the same segments as packed bytes — the form every key consumer (nighantu_khip, nighantu_antah, khand_tul) actually takes. Passing a nighantu_kunjika segment straight to a byte-key consumer compiles and silently compares the wrong bytes (the R14 trap).

column6: nighantu_kunjika_ashtak(m, out)nighantu_kunjika_ashtak(m, out) — R17. Same segments as nighantu_kunjika, but PACKED BYTES: [len-byte, bytes..., len-byte, bytes...], one length byte followed by the key's bytes, no terminator. Returns the key count, which equals nighantu_maap(m). Caller allocates cap * 33 bytes (each key is <= 32 bytes plus 1 length byte; at most cap keys). Keys are stored as packed bytes inside the map, so this is a straight byte copy — no unpack/pack round-trip. Segments can be passed directly to nighantu_khip / nighantu_antah / khand_tul with no repacking; that is the whole point (see nighantu_kunjika note above).

column6: layer: alloc R38: a formatter that cannot allocate its scratch writes only the terminator and returns 0. Number and string formatting on BYTE strings (packed bytes, explicit lengths, `khand` idiom): every function writes packed bytes into `out` with a 0 terminator and returns the byte count. This is the modern idiom; the older `lib/vakyank.smlib` works on CELL arrays (mala of char codes) and has no width/alignment/grouping/fixed-decimal/util_chinha surface — roop is the formatting module, vakyank is the conversion module. Do not mix the representations: roop outputs are bytes (read with char_at), vakyank outputs are cells (read with [i]). Defaults, stated once here and at each function: - Bases: no prefix unless the _pre / flags form is used. - Grouping: roop_varg defaults to INDIAN grouping (12,34,567). - Rounding: roop_sthir rounds HALF AWAY FROM ZERO (2.5 -> 3, -2.5 -> -3). - Centre padding: the extra pad byte goes RIGHT. - INT64_MIN (-2^63) is handled: |MIN| = 2^63 does not fit in int64, so the digit writers split it (hi/lo) instead of negating it. Every int64 value works. - roop_sthir is exact while |x| * 10^places < 2^52; beyond that the +0.5 rounding step is below float precision. |x| * 10^places must fit in int64. places is clamped to 0..9. All signatures stay within the 6-argument cap. --- integer digits (private helper) --- roop_ank(v, out) — write the decimal digits of |v| (no util_chinha) into out as packed bytes. Returns the digit count. Internal; the public formatters below build on it.

column6: layer: core Sutram has no 2-D array type, so a matrix is a FLAT `kosh dasham` of m*n elements in row-major order, with the dimensions passed explicitly: A[i][j] == a[i * n + j] for an m x n matrix CONTRACT for output matrices: the caller must have pushed m*n elements already. A kosh's capacity is not its length, so out[i] is out of bounds until an element exists. Functions here never `kosh_push` a parameter — the compiler rejects that, correctly, because the pointer is passed by value. Inputs are read-only. Outputs are written in place and are visible to the caller. --------------------------------------------------------------- element access helpers (flat index) --------------------------------------------------------------- samanvaya_akar_na(m, n, len) - R37: 1 when an m x n shape does NOT fit len elements (or m or n is negative), else 0. It divides, never multiplies, so it holds for every m and n: m x n fits exactly when n == 0 or m <= len / n.

column6: layer: alloc R38: an operation that cannot allocate its scratch returns -1, out unchanged (rakh_sam too). R39: scratch is sized from the set itself (a[0]), never from the caller's cap argument. A set IS a map (`lib/nighantu.smlib`) with a dummy value of 1: membership is nighantu_antah, iteration is nighantu_kunjika_ashtak (R17: packed-byte segments, passed straight to the byte-key map functions with no repacking). ELEMENTS ARE BYTE STRINGS — the same choice as `lib/nighantu.smlib` keys: a caller passes a literal directly ("apple"), with an explicit length. Do NOT pass char-code (qword-cell) arrays here. Inherited from map: keys longer than 32 bytes are truncated to 32 on every operation, consistently. CAPACITY: a set's capacity is fixed at rakh_srij and stored in the buffer (m[0]). Set operations that write into `out` read out's capacity from out[0], so the caller MUST pass a rakh_srij'd buffer with room for the result: cap + bcap for union, cap for difference, min(cap, bcap) for intersection. If `out` is too small, nighantu_khip silently drops the overflowing elements (map's full-table behaviour) and the returned size will be smaller than the true result — size the output generously and check the returned size. `out` for union / intersect / difference must be a FRESH, EMPTY set: the operations ADD into it and return nighantu_maap(out) afterwards. rakh_asti_upasamuh(a, ...) with an empty `a` is 1 (vacuous truth).

column6: layer: alloc Elements are QWORD CELLS (the mala/kosh convention), not byte strings. Users with byte strings store POINTERS (suchi_khip(l, ptr)); the caller keeps the pointed-to buffers alive. No mixing: every element here is a qword. dasham elements are NOT supported — an untyped parameter truncates a dasham argument to its integer part. Two handle layouts (do NOT mix families on one handle): - list / stack handle: header [len, cap, data_ptr]; data is a separate cell array. The HANDLE address is stable across growth — only the data pointer inside it moves. - queue handle: header [len, cap, data_ptr, head]; a RING BUFFER (see avali_pravesh). queue_* on a list handle (or list_* on a queue handle) reads the wrong header and corrupts memory. Growth rule: when len == cap, capacity DOUBLES, a new data array is allocated, elements are copied in logical order, and the header's data pointer is updated. The old data array is NOT freed — the language has no deallocation primitive, so growth leaks the previous array. Capacity never shrinks. Allocation failure: if nirmmita returns 0 during growth, the operation returns 0 (or ok[0] = 0) and the structure is UNCHANGED. suchi_srij returns 0 if either allocation fails. Out-of-bounds reads: suchi_grah returns 0 for i outside [0, len). 0 is a legal stored value, so check suchi_maap first when it matters. suchi_sangrah / suchi_nivesh / suchi_apanay return 1 ok / 0 out of bounds (or allocation failure for insert). chay_apanay / chay_avalok / avali_nishkas / avali_avalok return the value and set ok[0] (a 1-cell mala) to 1 on success, 0 when empty — the value alone cannot signal emptiness. All signatures stay within the 6-argument cap.

column6: layer: core Built on `vartani_aayam` and `char_at`, both verified to honour their arguments. R52 audit: `char_code(s, i)` already honours i in the compiler; a one-argument `char_code(s)` remains a compatible alias for the first byte. This library continues to call `char_at(s, i)` as before, without changing its API. ASCII only for the character predicates; multi-byte UTF-8 is not split. SLICE-BOUNDARY RULES (WS4, R23 audit): the older byte-string functions below (varna_maap, gan_swar, gan_akshar, anwesh_akshar, asti_sarv_ank, varna_sam) scan to the NUL terminator and are WRONG on slices — a slice has no terminator at its end. Use the explicit-length khand_* forms on slices. varna_pratisthap's repl is 0-terminated; see the strb.smlib header for why and for the khand_pratilip workaround. The (s, i) char predicates take no length: the caller keeps i in bounds.
